# Precedent: Progressive Disclosure and Expert Speed

How products keep the common path simple while giving frequent users speed. Observed 2026-09-24;
IDs refer to `research/observations/`.

---

### Google Flights — compact secondary options
`G1` · https://www.google.com/travel/flights · rendered
- **What works:** trip type, passengers, and cabin sit as small defaulted dropdowns above the main
  fields; only where-from, where-to, and dates are prominent.
- **Lesson:** secondary options stay visible but quiet, defaulted to the common answer.

### Airbnb mobile — search pill that expands
`ABm1` · https://www.airbnb.com/ · rendered 375×812
- **What works:** the whole search form is folded into one large tap target.
- **Lesson:** disclose the full form only when the user commits to searching.

### Stripe Docs — choose a path in place
`SD1 SD2` · https://docs.stripe.com/payments/accept-a-payment · rendered
- **What works:** tabs and a segmented control reconfigure one page for the reader's integration;
  an early callout routes non-developers away.
- **Lesson:** ask the branching question once, early, and adapt the content.

### Notion — slash commands, handles, markdown
`NO1 NO2 NO3` · https://www.notion.com/help/writing-and-editing-basics · documentation
- **What works:** "/" menu at the cursor for everyone; markdown shortcuts for experts; a hover handle
  that is both drag and menu.
- **Caution:** hover-only handles need keyboard and touch equivalents.

### GitHub — go to file
`GH3` · https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills · rendered
- **What works:** file search beside the branch picker, where file-finding begins.

### Grafana — shortcut shown in search
`GF4` · https://play.grafana.org/ · rendered
- **What works:** the search field shows its keyboard shortcut (⌘+K), teaching the fast path.

### TradingView — expert toolbars
`TV1 TV2` · https://www.tradingview.com/chart/ · rendered
- **Trade-off:** all tools visible as unlabeled icons: fast for experts, opaque for newcomers.
- **Lesson:** unlabeled density is a deliberate expert choice; it needs tooltips and a learning path.

### MDN — table of contents
`MD1` · https://developer.mozilla.org/ · rendered
- **What works:** every page lists the same sections so experts jump straight to "Browser compatibility".

### Linear — views over the same work
`LC1` · https://linear.app/docs/conceptual-model · documentation
- **What works:** views are saved lenses on the same issues, not new objects.
- **Lesson:** power comes from new ways to see, not new things to manage.

### ChatGPT — one suggestion
`CG3` · https://chatgpt.com/ · rendered
- **What works:** a single "What can you do?" chip instead of a grid of examples.
- **Lesson:** a small, optional hint beats a wall of onboarding.

---

## Summary rules

1. Common path prominent; secondary options visible, quiet, and defaulted.
2. Branching questions early, in place, answered once.
3. Teach shortcuts where they apply (in search fields, tooltips, menus).
4. Expert density is valid for expert audiences; provide labels or tooltips as the ramp.
